tvs.title_bl1_about: Lip tattoo – a great alternative to lipstick
tvs.text_bl1_about: If you use lipstick, gloss or lip liner every day, you know how exhausting it is to check your lips every hour and reapply after every meal and throughout the day. A permanent lip tattoo is an excellent alternative. Besides an always-made-up look, lip micropigmentation lets you hide imperfections in the area, correct the shape, visually add volume and eliminate asymmetry. Even if you don't wear cosmetics but want to refresh your look, go for aquarelle lips. Pink, lush, softly full lips are always attractive. You'll not only transform your appearance, giving it a fresh, polished look, but you'll also feel more confident. Whatever the situation and whatever you're doing, your lips will always keep their color and glow.

tvs.text-bl-seo-2:
What are the benefits of a semi-permanent lip tattoo?

First of all, it looks beautiful. Your lips look natural and effortless and need no extra care. If you like, you can add a clear lip gloss. Softly pigmented lips draw attention, while the tint gives them freshness and volume and makes them look well cared for. Visually expressive lips make the whole face look neat and polished. Even after a night out partying, a tanning session or a swim in the pool, your lips keep their look. Beyond aesthetics, permanent lip makeup:
hides imperfections: scars, marks, cold sore traces, freckles. Absolutely any flaw becomes invisible. No more covering them with a thick layer of lipstick or lip liner;
corrects the shape. What's more, you don't need beauty injections. Your lips will look fuller, plumper and more sensual. You can define your Cupid's bow, visually enlarge your upper lip, your lower lip or both, lift drooping lip corners or hide fine lines.
You can get all these benefits from a single procedure that takes up to 2 hours.

Main stages of lip micropigmentation

First, the artist gives you a consultation, answers your questions and selects the right pigment. The pigment should be slightly darker than the shade you've chosen, because it lightens during healing; that way you end up with exactly the shade you originally asked for. How the sketch is made depends on the technique. For example, with the aquarelle technique no sketch is drawn. It isn't needed, because the artist may go only half a millimeter beyond your natural lip line, visually enlarging the shape. For an ombré lip tattoo, a sketch is created by outlining the edges with a pencil or pen so that the pigment doesn't spread beyond them. This creates even proportions, and the client can see what her lips will look like at the end of the session. Before the procedure begins, an initial anesthetic is applied, followed by a 10–20 minute wait for it to take effect and fully numb the area. During the procedure, a secondary anesthetic is applied to relieve pain, redness and swelling. At the end, the artist will give you aftercare advice and schedule your touch-up appointment.

Touch-up after lip pigmentation

If you want excellent results and a color that lasts longer, you'll need a touch-up. It ensures your lips are fully saturated with color, keeps the effect lasting and eliminates any flaws. This is especially true if a cold sore appears after the procedure and leaves a small wound: the pigment will come away from that spot along with the regenerating skin, so the area needs to be retouched.

What you should know about lip micropigmentation

Lip micropigmentation has contraindications. These include insulin-dependent diabetes, HIV, epilepsy, mental disorders, skin inflammation on the lips, cold sores (labial herpes), pregnancy and breastfeeding. Menstruation is not a contraindication. If you feel unwell or have a fever or high blood pressure, it's advisable to reschedule the procedure.

Lip pigmentation doesn't fully replace Botox or hyaluronic acid injections if you want to add significant volume to your lips. It gives a visual enhancement by choosing the right pigment shade and placing it just over the natural lip line. That said, tattooing and beauty injections can be combined. The Botox treatment comes first, and once the product has settled under the skin, the lip tattoo procedure can be done. Before booking an appointment, we recommend consulting your artist.

Affordable lip micropigmentation in Bucharest can be a great way to feel feminine and look well-groomed. Choose the technique that flatters you most, and our studio will guarantee a precise and safe application.

migx_questions.questions-title: What lip tattoo techniques are there, and how do I choose?
migx_questions.questions-text: The most popular techniques are aquarelle and ombré. Aquarelle lip tattooing uses nude, pastel shades with delicate pigmentation. The ombré technique can use intense, fairly bright colors, applied as a denser shade. Ombré can be done with or without a contour.

migx_questions.questions-title: How long does aquarelle lip micropigmentation last?
migx_questions.questions-text: Up to 2 years, depending on how you care for your lips after the procedure, your lifestyle and your body's individual characteristics.

migx_questions.questions-title: How is aquarelle lip pigmentation different from other techniques?
migx_questions.questions-text: The key feature of an aquarelle lip tattoo is the choice of light shades and delicate pigmentation. As a result, your lips look fresh and natural. They have a soft pink tint, with no bold color that would require mascara and extra makeup to balance it. Your lips will look healthy and fresh. The only drawback of aquarelle lips is that this technique doesn't cover a bluish tinge of the skin and doesn't add volume, since no contour is used.

migx_questions.questions-title: Can lip micropigmentation cause cold sores (herpes)?
migx_questions.questions-text: The procedure doesn't cause herpes, because herpes is a viral infection that usually lies dormant in the body. When your immune system is weakened, the virus becomes active and shows up as a blister on the lips. During cosmetic tattooing the skin of the lips is traumatized, which can trigger an outbreak. So if you know you're prone to cold sores, it's recommended to take antiviral (antiherpetic) medication before and after the procedure to reduce the chance of blisters around the lips. Even if a cold sore does appear, it isn't harmful or dangerous. Once it has cleared and the skin has fully recovered, a touch-up can be done and the spot where the sore was can be covered.

migx_questions.questions-title: Can I get a lip tattoo during pregnancy?
migx_questions.questions-text: Lip tattooing is contraindicated during pregnancy and breastfeeding, since it is performed using an anesthetic.
